title: Extension of invertible modules across a factorial complement
statement: Let $Z$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and $U\subseteq Z$ an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume that for every $z\in Z\setminus U$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is a unique factorization domain, meaning an integral domain in which every nonzero nonunit factors as a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and unit factors. Every invertible $\mathcal O_U$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] has an extension: there are an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\widetilde M$ and an isomorphism $\widetilde M|_U\simeq M$. No density, integrality, separatedness, or uniqueness is assumed.

proof.text: First establish the local construction for any open $V$ with $U\subseteq V\subseteq Z$ and any invertible module $N$ on $V$. Let $W$ be an affine open of $Z$ and put $T=V\cap W$. Both $V$ and $T$ are locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc] to $V\hookrightarrow Z$: its inverse image $T$ of the affine open $W$ is quasi-compact. Thus $T$ is Noetherian and admits an open immersion into the affine scheme $W$. These are exactly the hypotheses needed for the quasi-affine divisor presentation, even when $V$ and $Z$ are not quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module, local divisor construction and final gluing paragraph; the transfinite construction below supplies explicit coherent choices instead of the source's Zorn ordering.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-quasiaffine-line-effective-divisor] choose an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset T$ with $N|_T\simeq\mathcal O_T(D)$. For $w\in W\setminus T$ one has $w\notin V$, hence $w\notin U$, so $\mathcal O_{W,w}=\mathcal O_{Z,w}$ is a UFD. Since $W$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-sfb-cartier-extension-factorial-complement] gives an effective Cartier divisor $E\subset W$ with $E\cap T=D$. Set $P=\mathcal O_W(E)$ using [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. This is invertible and $P|_T\simeq\mathcal O_T(D)$: on a neighbourhood where the ideal of $E$ is $f\mathcal O_W$, its dual is the free module with generator dual to $f$, and restricting this presentation gives the dual of the ideal of $D$. The identifications agree on overlaps because both use the same ideal inclusions. We have obtained an isomorphism $a:P|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_T$.

proof.text: Choose a set-indexed affine open cover $(W_\alpha)_{\alpha<\kappa}$ of $Z$ and well-order its index set. Put $V_\alpha=U\cup\bigcup_{\gamma<\alpha}W_\gamma$ for $\alpha\leq\kappa$. Starting with $N_0=M$, construct invertible modules $N_\alpha$ on $V_\alpha$ and isomorphisms $q_{\beta\alpha}:N_\alpha|_{V_\beta}\xrightarrow{\sim}N_\beta$ for $\beta\leq\alpha$, with $q_{\alpha\alpha}=1$ and $q_{\delta\alpha}=q_{\delta\beta}\circ(q_{\beta\alpha}|_{V_\delta})$. The following successor and limit constructions give the recursion, with all choices made in a sufficiently large fixed universe. Only a set of stages is used.

source.place: Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module, local divisor construction and final gluing paragraph; the transfinite construction below supplies explicit coherent choices instead of the source's Zorn ordering.

proof.text: At a successor stage apply steps 1 and 2 with $V=V_\alpha$, $N=N_\alpha$, and $W=W_\alpha$. On the two-open cover $V_{\alpha+1}=V_\alpha\cup W_\alpha$, glue $N_\alpha$ and $P$ using $a$ and $a^{-1}$ on their intersection, and identity maps for equal indices. Every cocycle equation is an inverse or identity equation. The module-gluing theorem [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing], applied to the Zariski site with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{V_{\alpha+1}}$, supplies $N_{\alpha+1}$ and in particular $q_{\alpha,\alpha+1}$. It is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module], since on each member of the cover it is locally free of rank one; these trivializations also give quasi-coherence, since the local models are structure sheaves. For $\beta<\alpha$ define $q_{\beta,\alpha+1}=q_{\beta\alpha}\circ(q_{\alpha,\alpha+1}|_{V_\beta})$. Associativity and the earlier compatibility equations give all the new compatibility equations.

source.place: Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module, local divisor construction and final gluing paragraph; the transfinite construction below supplies explicit coherent choices instead of the source's Zorn ordering.

proof.text: At a nonzero limit stage $\lambda\leq\kappa$, the set-indexed family $(V_\beta)_{\beta<\lambda}$ covers $V_\lambda$. For $\beta\leq\gamma<\lambda$ the overlap is $V_\beta$; use the transition $q_{\beta\gamma}^{-1}:N_\beta\to N_\gamma|_{V_\beta}$, and the inverse transition for reversed indices. The induction equation for the $q$'s gives the cocycle equation on a triple after sorting its three indices; inverse cancellation gives every other ordering. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] on the Zariski site of $V_\lambda$ to obtain $N_\lambda$ and comparison maps $q_{\beta\lambda}$. The overlap equation in that theorem says exactly $q_{\beta\lambda}=q_{\beta\gamma}\circ(q_{\gamma\lambda}|_{V_\beta})$. The module is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module], because near each point it is isomorphic to one of the invertible $N_\beta$; the same local trivializations give quasi-coherence. This completes the limit construction; no comparison map is inferred from density or uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module, local divisor construction and final gluing paragraph; the transfinite construction below supplies explicit coherent choices instead of the source's Zorn ordering.

proof.text: The recursion now reaches $V_\kappa=Z$. Take $\widetilde M=N_\kappa$ and the isomorphism $q_{0\kappa}:\widetilde M|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. If the affine cover is empty then $Z=U=\varnothing$ and take $\widetilde M=M$; if $U=Z$ one can take $M$ immediately. The construction also permits $U=\varnothing$, disconnected schemes and empty intersections. It proves existence with precisely the given hypotheses.

The statement matches Stacks 0BD9 (divisors.tex lemma-extend-invertible-module) hypothesis by hypothesis. Step 1: T=V∩W is quasi-compact by lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc (01OX) and locally Noetherian by the remark in pqf-def-locnoeth, so T is Noetherian and open in an affine scheme; no affine-intersection assumption (E1 fine). Step 2: 0AYM's quasi-affine clause (I checked the source line 'we may choose D'=∅') gives a single divisor D. 0BD8 applies with X=W and V=T, because points of W∖T are outside U and have UFD local rings. O_W(E)|_T≅O_T(D) by restricting the ideal sheaf. Steps 3–5: the transfinite recursion states its invariant (q_{αα}=1, q_{δα}=q_{δβ}∘q_{βα}|). At successor stages it glues along a and a^{-1}. At limit stages it glues with φ_{βγ}=q_{βγ}^{-1}, and the cocycle is the invariant. The output equation e_β=q_{βγ}∘e_γ| of lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing (04TR, arbitrary set covers, equal indices included) gives the invariant at λ, which I checked. The glued module is invertible because it is locally isomorphic to invertible modules. No density or uniqueness is used. Edge cases checked: U=Z, U=∅, Z=∅, disconnected Z, empty overlaps, non-quasi-compact Z; the quadric-cone vertex is correctly excluded by the UFD hypothesis. lean.statement: theorem exists_invertible_extension_of_factorial_complement {Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian Z] (U : Z.Opens) (hfactorial : ∀ z : Z, z ∉ U → IsDomain (Z.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ UniqueFactorizationMonoid (Z.presheaf.stalk z)) (M : U.toScheme.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : ∃ Mext : Z.Modules, Mext.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty ((tensorPullback U.ι).obj Mext ≅ M)
lean.note: Restriction is the canonical tensor pullback along U.ι, as recorded in the additional landed statement dependency def-pc-module-pullback. The factorial hypothesis is exactly IsDomain together with UniqueFactorizationMonoid, pointwise only outside U.
